protections: P1: an expansion budget (replacement count / expanded length) applied while entity references are substituted into text and attribute values; in the pinned code it is absent: replaceEntitiesValue does unbounded global replaces over the DOCTYPE, built-in, external, HTML/numeric and amp tables (src/xmlparser/OrderedObjParser.js:439-459). A (DOCTYPE entities) and B (numeric/HTML references) are both closed by one function-wide budget here.

P2: limits on what a DOCTYPE may declare (per-entity value size and number of entities); in the pinned code it is absent: every internal entity without '&' is stored with no size or count check (src/xmlparser/DocTypeReader.js:24-35, 113-116, 170-187).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: attribute values look like a separate, smaller channel than element text
a numeric character reference turns into output shorter than its input and only runs when htmlEntities is on (off by default), so it does not look like 'expansion'
these are the five predefined XML entities, which are required by the spec and map one-to-one onto a single character
values containing '&' are already dropped at declaration, so nested expansion looks impossible; the chained form is also a must-keep-working spec case
values registered through addEntity come from the developer, not the document, so they look trusted
a single large entity value is just input-size-proportional; a solver who caps expansion at substitution time may consider declaration size irrelevant
declaring many entities does not grow output; the cost is a per-entity regex pass over every text and attribute value, which is easy to miss
the v6 parser is not exported and its DOCTYPE entity reader is broken, so it cannot be reached
a webpack build artefact that the build regenerates, not source

conflicts.what: A depth/no-re-expansion rule (one pass, never expand text produced by an expansion) closes T5 but breaks the spec case where '& ' with nbsp='writer;' must become 'Writer: Donald Duck.' (spec/entities_spec.js:228-269); the budget must cap chained output without forbidding the chain.

Counting every character reference against the same small budget as DOCTYPE entities refuses legitimate documents dense in </&/&#x..; (for example, escaped markup or CJK text). The budget for character references has to be generous or separate.

If limits are added as fields of processEntities, the boolean true default (OptionsBuilder.js:31) and the shallow Object.assign merge (OptionsBuilder.js:45) must still yield default limits; DocTypeReader's '!processEntities' (DocTypeReader.js:5) must keep treating false as 'skip validation'.
addEntity values such as 'gt' -> '<>' must keep working (spec/entities_spec.js:582-594); a rule rejecting or heavily capping external-entity output would break them.

fairness_risks: The chained DOCTYPE expansion ('& ' -> '&writer;' -> expanded) is pinned by spec/entities_spec.js:228-269 and must keep working; a strict single-pass or depth-1 rule contradicts it.

HTML numeric/hex references with htmlEntities:true must keep decoding, including out-of-range ones passing through literally (spec/entities_spec.js:426-480, src/xmlparser/OrderedObjParser.js:632-640); a count cap refuses legitimate reference-dense text.

The pinned code exposes no names or defaults for limit options (src/xmlparser/OptionsBuilder.js:2-42); hidden tests that set processEntities:{maxTotalExpansions,...} or expect specific default thresholds or error messages are unfair unless the report names them.
processEntities:true and processEntities:false must keep their current boolean meaning (src/xmlparser/OptionsBuilder.js:31, src/xmlparser/OrderedObjParser.js:441, src/xmlparser/DocTypeReader.js:5).
Developer-registered entities via addEntity (src/xmlparser/XMLParser.js:46-56) are a legitimate use that a document-level budget must not refuse at normal sizes.

design.why: Under the shared-guard rule, everything except T7/T8 and T9 collapses into one group: a single counter in replaceEntitiesValue (OrderedObjParser.js:439-459) closes T1-T6 together. That leaves two real independent groups plus a plumbing/coupled-value item (T9), short of 3 independent missing protections. If a third is needed anyway, the best fallback is T3 (deepseek: numeric refs are a contraction, off by default; this is exactly the historical incomplete fix), T5 (mimo/how-type: chained expansion that must stay working per spec 228-269 but be bounded), and T7 (declaration-size limit at a different file). T3 and T5 still share the replaceEntitiesValue fix site, so this is a 2-group stack with T9 as an optional coupled-value check. It beats T1/T2/T4/T6 picks because those are either easy or absorbed by the same counter with no distinct judgement. T10/T11 are unreachable or build artefacts and must not be scored.
